feladatok.cim: Email to Ms Josífková about a creative writing course
feladatok.helyzet: You are a university student and have found the following advertisement on the website of your university:

bekezdesek: As children, it is through stories that we begin to learn how the world works. As adults, we often need a story to design a strong presentation, create an effective social media post, apply for a job, or write an academic essay.
Course aim: to improve writing skills
• to enable you to sell your idea, concept, or product through a variety of narrative tools and methods;
• to enhance your English vocabulary, composition and writing style.
Young professionals and university students with at least an intermediate (B2) level of English.
Interested? And you don’t mind receiving homework before the course starts? Contact our co-ordinator, Andrea Josífková, by email: info@europeansummerschool.com

feladatok.teendo: Write an email of 120-150 words to Ms Josífková in which you
iranyito_szempontok: introduce yourself, and say why you think improving your writing skills will be advantageous for your studies/future job,
ask about the details of the homework you will receive before the course starts,
ask about the date(s) and duration of the course, and the course fee.

feladatok.cim: Comment to Emily about photos posted by her mother
feladatok.helyzet: You’ve found the following post in your group chat with your class.

bekezdesek: Hey guys, the most irritating thing has happened, and it’s driving me crazy.

My mum had her birthday and we had a family get-together at the weekend, where everyone took a lot of pictures, of course. I didn’t think much of it, goofing around with my cousins as usual. To my horror, my mum posted a lot of these photos on social media the next day. We all look ridiculous, especially me. I was wearing no make-up, and I never realized the dress I was wearing looked so hideous!

I confronted my mum and told her to delete the pictures immediately, because she had no right to post these without my consent, but she says she is my mother, I’m a minor, it was her birthday, and she can share photos of her own party if she likes. We had a huge fight, I even begged her to delete the photos, but she won’t budge, and we are still not speaking.

What shall I do? I’ll hack her account if I have to, but I can’t have my photos appear on all her social media with me looking like that. It was ok when I was little, I didn’t have a say in it then, but shouldn’t she take my feelings into account now that I’m 17???

feladatok.teendo: Write a comment of 200-250 words to Emily’s post, in which you tell her
iranyito_szempontok: whether anything similar has ever happened to you or anyone you know,
whether you think parents should post pictures of their children on social media,
at what age you think a person should be able to control what others post about them,
what you think she should do in this situation.
